Let $g(x)=2-5x$ and $f(g(x))=g(x{)}^{3}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =({g}^{3}{)}^{′}=3{g}^{2}, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(2-5x{)}^{′}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =3{g}^{2}\cdot (-5) \\  & =-15(2-5x{)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
